ai.title: Add top-freebuff-users.ts script for usage analysis
ai.summary: New scripts/top-freebuff-users.ts queries database to list top Freebuff-only users by message count within configurable time window. Excludes users with base2 or base2-max messages to isolate pure Freebuff usage. Reports email, messages, credits, cost, and last active timestamp. Flags users with ≥50 messages for high-usage review.

eli5.text: The team added a new behind-the-scenes script that scans the database for people using only the Freebuff model, ignoring anyone who has also used base2 or base2-max. It produces a sorted list showing email, message count, credits used, cost, and last activity for each free-only user, and separately flags anyone with 50 or more messages for closer review. This is internal tooling used today by whoever runs the script, not something visible to users.

ai.title: Fix Enter key detection in terminals sending linefeed
ai.summary: Added `terminal-enter-detection.ts` to treat `linefeed` keys as Enter when no `return` key is observed. Updated `chat-input-bar.tsx`, `multiline-input.tsx`, `use-chat-keyboard.ts`, and `keyboard-actions.ts` to use `isLinefeedActingAsEnter` and `markReturnKeySeen`. This resolves submission failures in niche Linux terminals that send `\n` instead of `\r` for Enter.

eli5.text: On some Linux computers, pressing Enter didn't submit your message because their terminal sent a slightly different signal. Now, if the app hasn't seen the normal Enter signal, it treats this alternate signal as Enter instead. This means you can reliably send messages while typing in the terminal, even on those unusual setups. It's already live today.

ai.title: Get Started page
ai.summary: Added `freebuff/web/src/app/get-started/page.tsx` and `get-started-client.tsx`. Detects OS for install command `npm install -g freebuff`. Displays editor logos for VS Code, Cursor, IntelliJ, Terminal in `freebuff/web/public/logos/`.

eli5.text: Visitors to the new Get Started page on Freebuff's website are automatically shown the correct installation command for their operating system and can see icons for popular code editors like VS Code, Cursor, IntelliJ, and Terminal. The page is now live and publicly accessible; no login or extra setup is required to view or use it. The editor icons are displayed as image files alongside the installation instructions, making it easier for newcomers to recognize which tools are supported.
